transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doc. Well, I guess what brought me in is... people just keep saying I'm not listening. 

Like, my supervisor at work, or my wife at home. They'll be talking straight to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught half of what they said. So I end up having to ask them to say it all over again. It's just getting to be a real problem.
Does your partner ever mention that you snore loudly or seem to stop breathing or gasp for air while you're asleep?

No, she hasn't said anything like that. I mean, I might snore a little bit if I've got a cold or something, but she's never mentioned me stopping breathing or gasping or anything serious like that. She's a pretty light sleeper, so I figure she'd let me know if I was doing that.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel down or sad or anything like that. I still like doing the things I usually do. It's just... I just have a hard time staying focused on them, you know? But I wouldn't say I'm depressed or losing interest.

When people say you're not listening, is it because you genuinely can't hear or understand what they said clearly, or is it more that your mind wanders and you miss parts of the conversation even though you heard the words fine?

No, my hearing is fine. I can hear the words clear as day. It's definitely that second thing you said. 

My mind just... takes off somewhere else. Like, I'll be looking right at my wife, hearing her voice, but suddenly I'm thinking about a machine on the production floor or something I need to fix out in the garage. Then I kind of snap back and realize I have no idea what she actually just said to me. The words just didn't stick.

Thinking back, did you have similar struggles with staying focused or getting distracted when you were a kid in school, or is this something that's really only started happening in recent months or years?

No, it's definitely not a new thing. I was like this even as a kid. I mean, teachers were always moving my seat around because I just couldn't stay put. I was always calling out answers in class, and... well, I got into trouble a lot for butting into other kids' work. All of that was way back, definitely before middle school even. So yeah, it's been like this pretty much as long as I can remember.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset history with both inattentive symptoms (mind wandering, missing conversation details) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (couldn't stay seated, blurting answers, interrupting others) since before middle school strongly supports ADHD combined presentation. This childhood-onset pattern rules out F06.7 (mild neurocognitive disorder due to another medical condition), which would require an acquired, later-onset cognitive decline rather than a lifelong developmental pattern.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, pervasive inattentive symptoms (mind wandering, missing parts of conversations, forgetting instructions) that began in childhood (pre-middle school) along with hyperactive-impulsive behaviors (couldn't stay seated, blurting answers, interrupting). Symptoms have persisted into adulthood and cause functional impairment at work and home. Sleep apnea was ruled out (no snoring, gasping, or witnessed apneas), and depressive disorder was ruled out (no anhedonia or low mood). The combination of early-onset inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms with chronic course and functional impairment supports a diagnosis of ADHD (ICD-10 F90.0, Disturbance of Activity and Attention).
